Over every variant and contact setting (the worst case is named). The B7 pulse is an ENVELOPE: the largest bus surplus of one run with that run's own span, beside the largest peak powers over all runs (often other runs); the worst-energy run's own peaks are in their own column.

Ceilings on the mechanical energy the drives can take net while powered (DESK, energy balance on the simulated motion, before the linkage and copper losses; max over the sit's runs): the powered-phase ceiling is the kinetic energy at the stop input plus the potential energy released before the cut; it holds for any sit that reaches the same height before the cut. It bounds the drives' net take (what they brake less what they put in), not their gross braking: a drive's own positive work can be braked out again, so the gross braking at the joints can exceed it, and so could the bus surplus of a routine that pushes and brakes in turn. The full-drop ceiling adds the drop after the cut, for a routine that lowered the body all the way while powered. Seconds: of the two 50 W resistors' 100 W continuous rating.

Bus capacitance (DESK): 0.128 J per mF from 50.0 to 52.5 V, 0.168 J per mF from 49.2 V, 0.263 J per mF from 50.0 to 55 V; capacitance that alone holds the worst hard sit under 52.5 V: 22.8 mF, under 55 V: 11.1 mF.

Back-EMF threshold (DESK; output rpm at which a drive's line back-EMF reaches a bus held at that voltage; below it a drive with its bridge off pushes no current into a held bus, but into a decayed link it rectifies at any speed): X4-36-L 271 rpm at 42V, 318 rpm at 49.2V, 323 rpm at 50V; X6-60 134 rpm at 42V, 157 rpm at 49.2V, 159 rpm at 50V. From Kt instead, at 42 V: X4-36-L 273 rpm, X6-60 234 rpm. Peak drive speeds over every collapse: roll 50 rpm, pitch 68 rpm, front elbow 76 rpm, hind knee 77 rpm.

Pack charge acceptance: not given in the records; the ideal diodes block regen from the pack (hardware/triceratops_kickoff/PARTS_PREMIUM.md:311).
